one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall before 2026-11-01; Q1 FY27 (guide $3.80-4.20 core EPS, $10.6-11.4B revenue) is due mid/late December. Events inside the window: the FY26 10-K (late October; customer-concentration disclosure), late-October hyperscaler Q3 calls with 2027 capex commentary, Celestica and Flex prints, the FOMC and the 2026-11-03 midterms. Third-party trackers still point to 2027 growth (TrendForce: NVL72 rack shipments +50%+), so a capex cut on the calls is unlikely, but the stock already sold off 10% on a beat, which shows the market is pricing a deceleration. I see no reliable directional edge. The stock has retraced about 6% of the 9/30 drop, so I allow a slight drift: lognormal centred near $306 with a monthly sigma of ~13% (47%/3.5), tails a little fatter than lognormal.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28E core EPS $20.6 x 16.5x = $340) and FCF yield (FY28E adj. FCF ~$1.75B at a 5.25% yield over ~101M diluted shares = ~$330), weighted 50/50, giving ~$335.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 core EPS ~$20.6 (rebuilt segment bridge: revenue $44.5B to ~$49.9B, +12%; core margin 6.1% to 6.3%; ~3% share shrink) x 16.5x

inputs_detail.value: Cloud/DC $17.5B (+52%), capital equipment $4.2B (+40%), networking/comms $3.9B (+15%), Regulated Industries $13.6B (+7%), Intelligent Devices & Robotics $5.3B (-2%, incl. Connected Living $2.3B, -15%)

inputs_detail.derivation: Cloud/DC +22% to ~$21.4B: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth slows to ~25-50% (UBS ~25%, TrendForce ~50% for nine CSPs) and NVL72 rack shipments grow 50%+ in 2027, but FY28 (Sep-27 to Aug-28) straddles UBS's 2028 slowdown to ~6%. New committed capacity supports it: Rowan County NC (1,181 jobs, ramp through early CY2027) and a second Marshall County MS site (1.5M sq ft, ~2,200 jobs, July 2026). Capital equipment +10%, networking +10%, Regulated Industries +5%, IDR flat.
The FY27 guide is 6.1% with a back-end-loaded ramp (45/55 H1/H2), so the FY27 exit rate runs above 6.1%. Capex is held at 1.5-2% of revenue. I take about half the implied exit-rate uplift.
$1.06B of FY26 buybacks and a ~$1.4B remaining authorization against a ~$32B market cap. Diluted shares were 106.0M in Q4 FY26.

17.55 x (3.14/2.71 operating-income growth) x 1/0.97 for share shrink gives ~$21.0. I haircut it ~$0.4 for higher interest on a working-capital-funded balance sheet (FY26 interest and other of $296M).

Flex is at ~25x its raised FY27 guide ($116.61 against a $4.58 midpoint), so my round-1 anchor of 18.2x was stale. JBL is at 17.3x its FY27 guide now, and its 5-year average is ~14x. At the horizon the market will be pricing FY29 into a decelerating capex cycle (UBS: 2028 capex growth ~6%), and the payables-funded working capital argues for a discount to Flex. 16.5x sits between JBL's history and the peer level.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 adj. FCF ~$1.75B / 5.25% = ~$33.3B equity value; ~101M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Grows less than EPS: working capital stays heavy (FY26 receivables +$2.4B, inventory +$2.7B, funded by +$8B of payables) and the Mississippi and North Carolina site fit-outs absorb cash.

Spot implies ~5.0% on FY27 FCF. Net debt is $1.64B, not the ~$2.3B I used in round 1, which removes part of my reason for a 5.5% yield. The working-capital intensity still justifies a small premium yield.
Debt $499M current plus $2,880M long-term, less $1,739M cash at 2026-08-31.
106.0M diluted in Q4 FY26 less ~3-4% from buybacks.

bear.story: In this case hyperscaler capex digestion arrives early: UBS-style deceleration toward ~6% growth in 2028 is priced by mid-2027, and ASIC programs shift share. Cloud/DC growth stalls in FY28, the new MS and NC capacity runs underutilised, FY28 EPS sits near $17, and the multiple falls to ~12x. Macro recession odds are no longer used to size this case.

base.story: Jabil delivers the FY27 guide ($44.5B, 6.1%, $17.55) with its usual modest beat. The FY28 outlook (late Sept 2027) implies ~$20.6 core EPS on ~12% revenue growth led by cloud/DC, and the stock holds ~16.5x, still a discount to Flex.

bull.story: 2027 capex lands near TrendForce's $1.3T, VR200 rack volumes pull through, and the Mississippi site ramps quickly. Jabil repeats its +13-19% beat against the initial full-year guide (FY27 EPS ~$19.5), FY28 is guided above $22, and the multiple moves toward 20x, between JBL's mid-2026 levels and Flex. The stock retakes the $429 high.

thesis_break_reason: $215 is ~12x the $17.55 FY27 guide and ~29% below spot, well under the $284-287 lows that held through the Jul-Sep 2026 AI-hardware selloff and the post-print drop. A close there would most likely mean the market is pricing a guide cut: a hyperscaler program pause or loss, capex digestion pulled into 2027, or a working-capital unwind as the $14.4B of payables normalises. Ordinary volatility would not get it there. I keep $215 rather than the supervisor's $210: the difference is within noise, and $215 matches my bear-tail centre.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META); Celestica and Flex results
Jabil Q1 FY27 earnings (guide $3.80-4.20 core EPS, $10.6-11.4B revenue)
Rowan County NC ramp completes (early CY2027) and Marshall County MS data-center site starts up; hiring pace is a leading indicator

key_uncertainties: 2027-28 hyperscaler capex path: TrendForce sees ~$1.3T in 2027 (+~50%), UBS sees growth slowing to ~25% in 2027 and ~6% in 2028. FY28 straddles the slowdown.
Cloud/DC concentration: $17.5B of revenue (+52%), with a second hyperscaler above 10% of revenue; ASIC programs shifting share among hyperscalers.
Utilisation and start-up costs of new capacity (NC 1,181 jobs; MS 1.5M sq ft and ~2,200 jobs) if demand pauses.
Working-capital intensity: FY26 growth funded by +$8B of payables, and FCF flat on +24% revenue.
Exit multiple: JBL's 5-year average is ~14x vs Flex at ~25x; each 1x is ~$20/share.
reasoning: Round 2. I corrected the facts the supervisor established. Net debt is $1.64B, not $2.3B. Networking/communications grows +15% in FY27; the +52% growth is in cloud/data center ($17.5B) and capital equipment grows +40%. Flex trades at ~25x, not 18.2x. The Kalshi 41% recession figure is unverified and no longer sizes my bear case. I rebuilt FY28 bottom-up from the segment guide: cloud/DC +22%, the rest low single digits, which gives revenue ~$49.9B (+12%). With a 6.3% margin and ~3% buybacks, FY28 core EPS is ~$20.6, essentially my round-1 figure, now on a correct bridge. On the supervisor's advice I spent the follow-up research on alternative data. (a) Jabil bought and is renovating a second Marshall County, MS site in July 2026: 1.5M sq ft, ~$119M, ~2,200 jobs for data-center infrastructure. Two sources confirm it (Area Development, WLBT). Together with NC (1,181 jobs; an AI server-rack engineering manager posting in Apr 2026) and Memphis/India, this shows Jabil is committing capacity for FY28 demand, not only FY27. (b) A job-postings aggregator shows ~1,774 open roles with 300+ added in the last 30 days (3 Oct 2026). That is consistent with expansion, but the counts are noisy and it is a single aggregator, so it does not move a number. (c) Supply-chain trackers: TrendForce expects NVL72 rack shipments to grow 50%+ in 2027 and nine-CSP capex near $1.3T. Against that, UBS models capex growth falling to ~25% in 2027 and ~6% in 2028, and Reuters reports investors positioning for slower spending growth. So the main bear risk is digestion around the horizon, when the market will be pricing FY29. Valuation: 16.5x x $20.6 = $340, raised from 16x because my peer anchor was stale, though still discounted to Flex for working-capital quality and cycle timing. A 5.25% FCF yield on ~$1.75B gives ~$330, a slightly lower yield because the net-debt correction removed part of my haircut. Fair value is ~$335, ~10% above spot. Distribution: an 86/14 mixture of lognormals, the main one with median $333 and sigma 0.36, plus a digestion/guide-cut tail at median $215 with sigma 0.40. Extreme tails are fattened slightly. That gives P(>=304) of ~0.54, a little higher than round 1. The scenarios bracket it: bear $205 (22%), base $340 (50%), bull $450 (28%). Where I differ from the supervisor: I use 16.5x rather than its ~16x cap, because new plant commitments for FY28 demand and Flex at 25x justify a bit more. I also keep the thesis break at $215. Limits: X/Twitter was not reachable, the UBS and $1.3T capex figures come from secondary snippets, and the job-count data is from one aggregator.
